notes.definition: Crude oil is a finite resource found in rocks, formed from the remains of an ancient biomass made mainly of plankton buried in mud. It is a mixture of a very large number of compounds, most of which are hydrocarbons, and most of these hydrocarbons are alkanes, which have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
explanation: Crude oil formed over millions of years from the remains of tiny sea organisms, mainly plankton. When they died they sank and were buried in mud. Layers of sediment built up on top, and the high temperature and pressure, with little oxygen, slowly changed the remains into crude oil. Crude oil is found trapped in porous rocks underground. Because it took millions of years to form and we are using it much faster than it could ever be replaced, crude oil is a finite (non-renewable) resource.

Crude oil is a mixture, not a single substance. It contains a very large number of different compounds that are not chemically bonded to each other, so they can be separated by physical methods. Most of the compounds in crude oil are hydrocarbons. A hydrocarbon is a compound made of hydrogen and carbon atoms only. Substances such as ethanol (C₂H₅OH) or glucose are not hydrocarbons, because they also contain oxygen.

Most of the hydrocarbons in crude oil belong to one family called the alkanes. All alkanes have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, where n is the number of carbon atoms. So an alkane with 5 carbon atoms has 2 × 5 + 2 = 12 hydrogen atoms: C₅H₁₂. Each member of the family differs from the next by CH₂. You only need to know the names of the first four alkanes: methane (CH₄), ethane (C₂H₆), propane (C₃H₈) and butane (C₄H₁₀). Any other alkane can be recognised from its formula.

The atoms in an alkane are held together by covalent bonds. Each carbon atom forms four covalent bonds and each hydrogen atom forms one. In alkanes every carbon to carbon bond is a single bond (C–C). Because each carbon is already bonded to as many hydrogen atoms as possible, alkanes are described as saturated hydrocarbons.

Alkanes can be shown by a molecular formula, such as C₂H₆, which tells you how many atoms of each element are in one molecule. They can also be shown by a displayed formula, which shows every atom and every covalent bond as a line. In a displayed formula of an alkane, each C has four lines coming from it and each H has one. Count the C and H atoms in a displayed formula to work out the molecular formula, then check it fits CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
keyFacts: Crude oil is a finite resource found in rocks.
Crude oil is the remains of an ancient biomass consisting mainly of plankton buried in mud.
Crude oil is a mixture of a very large number of compounds.
A hydrocarbon is a compound containing hydrogen and carbon atoms only.
Most hydrocarbons in crude oil are alkanes, general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
The first four alkanes are methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆, propane C₃H₈ and butane C₄H₁₀.
Alkanes contain only single C–C bonds, so they are saturated.
Each carbon atom forms 4 covalent bonds and each hydrogen atom forms 1.
Each alkane differs from the next one by a CH₂ unit.

keyTerms.definition: A finite resource found in rocks, made from the remains of ancient plankton; a mixture of a very large number of compounds, mostly hydrocarbons.
A resource that is not being made at a rate fast enough to replace what we use, so it will run out.
Two or more substances not chemically combined together, which can be separated by physical methods.
A compound made of hydrogen and carbon atoms only.
A saturated hydrocarbon with only single C–C bonds and the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
Containing only single carbon to carbon bonds, so no more hydrogen atoms can be added.
A diagram that shows every atom in a molecule and every covalent bond as a line.
A formula that shows the actual number of atoms of each element in one molecule, for example C₃H₈.

equations.name: General formula of the alkanes
equations.formula: number of H atoms = 2 × number of C atoms + 2

workedExamples.title: Using the general formula
workedExamples.question: An alkane has 9 carbon atoms. Write its molecular formula.
steps: The general formula of the alkanes is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

workedExamples.title: Working backwards from hydrogen atoms
workedExamples.question: An alkane molecule contains 26 hydrogen atoms. How many carbon atoms does it have?
workedExamples.answer: 12 carbon atoms, so the formula is C₁₂H₂₆.

workedExamples.title: Relative formula mass of an alkane
workedExamples.question: Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of butane, C₄H₁₀. (Ar: C = 12, H = 1)

workedExamples.title: Is it an alkane?
workedExamples.question: Which of these is an alkane: C₆H₁₂, C₆H₁₄ or C₆H₁₂O₆?
steps: C₆H₁₂O₆ contains oxygen, so it is not a hydrocarbon at all.
For n = 6, an alkane needs 2 × 6 + 2 = 14 hydrogen atoms.
C₆H₁₂ has only 12 hydrogen atoms, so it does not fit CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think crude oil is a single compound.
misconceptions.right: In fact crude oil is a mixture of a very large number of compounds, mostly hydrocarbons, which are not chemically joined to each other.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think any compound containing carbon and hydrogen is a hydrocarbon.
misconceptions.right: In fact a hydrocarbon contains hydrogen and carbon only. Ethanol, C₂H₅OH, contains oxygen so it is not a hydrocarbon.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think crude oil formed from dinosaurs.
misconceptions.right: In fact crude oil formed mainly from plankton (tiny sea organisms) buried in mud.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think 'saturated' means the alkane is dissolved in something.
misconceptions.right: In fact saturated means the molecule has only single C–C bonds, so it holds the maximum number of hydrogen atoms.

realWorld: Methane is the main compound in natural gas, used for cooking and heating homes.
Propane and butane are sold in cylinders as bottled gas (LPG) for camping stoves and barbecues.
Because crude oil is finite, scientists are developing alternatives such as biofuels and recycling plastics made from crude oil.
examTips: When drawing a displayed formula, check every C has exactly 4 bonds and every H has exactly 1.
To decide if a formula is an alkane, check it has only C and H, then check H = 2C + 2.
Learn the names and formulae of methane, ethane, propane and butane; for other alkanes you only need to use the general formula.
If asked how crude oil formed, mention plankton, buried in mud, and that it is finite because it takes millions of years to form.
summary: Crude oil is a finite resource formed from ancient plankton buried in mud.
It is a mixture of many compounds, mostly hydrocarbons.
Hydrocarbons contain hydrogen and carbon only.
Most hydrocarbons in crude oil are alkanes, CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
Methane, ethane, propane and butane are the first four alkanes.
Alkanes are saturated: they contain only single C–C bonds.

questions.question: What is crude oil mainly formed from?
options: Remains of dinosaurs buried in sand
Remains of plankton buried in mud
Remains of trees buried in swamps
markScheme: 1 mark: remains of plankton buried in mud
questions.explanation: Crude oil is the remains of an ancient biomass consisting mainly of plankton buried in mud. Trees in swamps formed coal, not crude oil, and dinosaurs are a common myth.

questions.question: Which statement about crude oil is correct?
options: It is a mixture of a very large number of compounds
markScheme: 1 mark: a mixture of a very large number of compounds
questions.explanation: Crude oil contains many different compounds, mostly hydrocarbons, that are not chemically joined. It is finite, not renewable.

questions.question: Which of these is the definition of a hydrocarbon?
options: A compound containing hydrogen and carbon only
A compound containing hydrogen, carbon and oxygen
A mixture of hydrogen gas and carbon
markScheme: 1 mark: compound of hydrogen and carbon only
questions.explanation: The word 'only' is essential. Compounds that also contain oxygen, such as ethanol, are not hydrocarbons. A hydrocarbon is a compound, not a mixture of the elements.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the displayed formula of propane.
What is the molecular formula of propane?
markScheme: 1 mark: C₃H₈
questions.explanation: Propane has 3 carbon atoms, so n = 3 and the number of H atoms is 2 × 3 + 2 = 8. C₂H₆ is ethane and C₄H₁₀ is butane.

questions.question: Which formula represents an alkane?
markScheme: 1 mark: C₅H₁₂
questions.explanation: For n = 5, an alkane has 2 × 5 + 2 = 12 hydrogen atoms. C₅H₁₁OH contains oxygen so it is not a hydrocarbon.

questions.question: Why are alkanes described as saturated?
options: They contain only single carbon to carbon bonds
They contain a carbon to carbon double bond
They are made of carbon atoms only
markScheme: 1 mark: only single C–C bonds
questions.explanation: Saturated means only single C–C bonds, so each carbon holds as many hydrogen atoms as possible. A C=C double bond would make it unsaturated.

questions.question: Which name matches the alkane with 4 carbon atoms?
markScheme: 1 mark: butane
questions.explanation: Meth = 1, eth = 2, prop = 3, but = 4 carbon atoms. Butane is C₄H₁₀.

questions.question: Why is crude oil described as a finite resource?
options: It is found in only one country
It cannot be separated into useful parts
It is being used up much faster than it can form
It is a mixture of compounds
markScheme: 1 mark: used faster than it forms / will run out
questions.explanation: Crude oil takes millions of years to form, so it is not replaced on a human timescale and will eventually run out. Being a mixture does not make it finite.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the displayed formula of ethane, C₂H₆.
How many covalent bonds are shown in Figure 1?
markScheme: 1 mark: 7
questions.explanation: There are 6 C–H bonds and 1 C–C bond, so 7 bonds in total. Forgetting the C–C bond gives 6.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows the first four members of the alkane family.
Two consecutive members of the alkane family differ by which group of atoms?
markScheme: 1 mark: CH₂
questions.explanation: Each extra carbon atom brings 2 extra hydrogen atoms (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ to Cₙ₊₁H₂ₙ₊₄), so neighbours differ by CH₂. For example ethane C₂H₆ and propane C₃H₈.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows the first four members of the alkane family.
An alkane has 8 carbon atoms.
How many hydrogen atoms does one molecule of this alkane contain?
markScheme: 1 mark: 18
questions.explanation: Use CₙH₂ₙ₊₂: 2 × 8 + 2 = 18, so the formula is C₈H₁₈.

questions.question:
Propane has the formula C₃H₈.
Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of propane.
Relative atomic masses (Ar): C = 12   H = 1
markScheme: 1 mark: 44
questions.explanation: 36 + 8 = 44. A common slip is to add 12 + 1 for each formula 'part' instead of multiplying by the number of atoms.

questions.question:
An alkane molecule contains 30 hydrogen atoms.
Calculate the number of carbon atoms in one molecule of this alkane.
markScheme: 1 mark: n = 14
questions.explanation: 2n = 28, so n = 14. The alkane is C₁₄H₃₀.

questions.question:
An alkane has 10 carbon atoms in each molecule.
Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of this alkane.
Relative atomic masses (Ar): C = 12   H = 1
markScheme: 1 mark: formula C₁₀H₂₂
questions.explanation: First work out the formula: H = 2 × 10 + 2 = 22, so C₁₀H₂₂. Then Mr = 10 × 12 + 22 × 1 = 142.

questions.question:
An alkane has a relative formula mass (Mr) of 72.
Calculate the number of carbon atoms in one molecule of this alkane.
Relative atomic masses (Ar): C = 12   H = 1
markScheme: 1 mark: n = 5
questions.explanation: Each alkane has mass 12n from carbon and 2n + 2 from hydrogen, so Mr = 14n + 2. Solving gives n = 5, which is C₅H₁₂ (Mr = 60 + 12 = 72).

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the displayed formula of a hydrocarbon.
Name the alkane shown in Figure 1.

markScheme: 1 mark: methane
questions.explanation: Methane has one carbon atom bonded to four hydrogen atoms. It is the simplest alkane and the main part of natural gas.

questions.question: State the general formula of the alkanes.
markScheme: 1 mark: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂
questions.explanation: For n carbon atoms there are 2n + 2 hydrogen atoms.

questions.question: Describe how crude oil was formed.
markScheme: 1 mark: remains of ancient biomass / plankton
1 mark: buried in mud (and changed over millions of years by heat and pressure)
questions.explanation: Crude oil formed from the remains of plankton that were buried in mud and slowly changed by heat and pressure over millions of years.

questions.question: Ethanol has the formula C₂H₅OH. Explain why ethanol is not a hydrocarbon.
markScheme: 1 mark: hydrocarbons contain hydrogen and carbon only
1 mark: ethanol also contains oxygen
questions.explanation: A hydrocarbon contains only hydrogen and carbon atoms. The O in C₂H₅OH means ethanol is not a hydrocarbon.

questions.question:
Describe the displayed formula of ethane, C₂H₆.
Give the number of C–H bonds and the number of C–C bonds in one molecule.
acceptedAnswers: two carbons each with three hydrogens
markScheme: 1 mark: two C atoms joined by a single bond, each bonded to three H atoms
1 mark: 6 C–H bonds and 1 C–C bond
questions.explanation: Ethane is H₃C–CH₃ in displayed form: each carbon has three H atoms and one bond to the other carbon, giving four bonds per carbon.

questions.question:
A student says:
'C₇H₁₄ is an alkane because it contains only carbon and hydrogen.'
Explain why the student is wrong.
markScheme: 1 mark: it is a hydrocarbon but does not fit CₙH₂ₙ₊₂
1 mark: an alkane with 7 C would have 16 H (C₇H₁₆)
questions.explanation: Being a hydrocarbon is not enough. For n = 7 the alkane formula is C₇H₁₆, so C₇H₁₄ has too few hydrogen atoms to be an alkane.

questions.question: Explain why crude oil can be separated into different substances by physical methods.
markScheme: 1 mark: crude oil is a mixture
1 mark: the compounds are not chemically combined with each other
questions.explanation: Because the compounds in a mixture are not bonded to one another, they keep their own properties, such as boiling point, and can be separated physically.

markScheme: 1 mark: each carbon atom forms four covalent bonds
1 mark: each hydrogen atom forms only one bond
1 mark: in CH₄ / C₂H₆ every carbon already has four bonds, so there is no bond available for another H (the formula would not fit CₙH₂ₙ₊₂)
questions.explanation: In methane and ethane every carbon bond is already used. An extra H atom would need a fifth bond on carbon, which is not possible.

questions.question:
A hydrocarbon has 18 carbon atoms and 36 hydrogen atoms in each molecule.
Is this hydrocarbon an alkane?
Give a reason for your answer.
markScheme: 1 mark: not an alkane
1 mark: alkane with 18 C has 2 × 18 + 2 = 38 H
questions.explanation: C₁₈H₃₆ has 2 fewer hydrogen atoms than the alkane C₁₈H₃₈, so it is not an alkane.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the displayed formula of butane.
The molecular formula of butane is C₄H₁₀.
Suggest one advantage of using a displayed formula rather than a molecular formula.
markScheme: 1 mark: displayed formula shows every bond / how the atoms are joined
1 mark: e.g. shows only single C–C bonds so it is saturated
questions.explanation: A molecular formula gives only the numbers of atoms. A displayed formula shows how they are joined, so you can see that all C–C bonds are single.

questions.question:
Describe what crude oil is and how it was formed.
Explain why crude oil is described as a finite resource.
markScheme: Indicative content: formed from remains of ancient biomass, mainly plankton; buried in mud; changed by heat and pressure over millions of years; found in rocks; mixture of a very large number of compounds; mostly hydrocarbons (mostly alkanes); finite because it is used much faster than it forms, so it will run out.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): clear description of formation and composition, with a correct explanation of finite.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements, e.g. made from dead sea creatures, or it will run out, with little linking.
questions.explanation: A full answer links the slow formation (millions of years) to why it cannot be replaced at the rate we use it, and states it is a mixture of mainly hydrocarbons.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows the formulae of four compounds, A, B, C and D.
Explain how you could decide whether each compound is an alkane.
Your answer should refer to:
• the definition of a hydrocarbon
• the general formula of the alkanes

markScheme: Indicative content: a hydrocarbon contains hydrogen and carbon only; C₂H₅OH contains oxygen so it is not a hydrocarbon and not an alkane; alkanes fit CₙH₂ₙ₊₂; C₃H₈: 2 × 3 + 2 = 8, so alkane (propane); C₆H₁₂: alkane would be C₆H₁₄, so not an alkane; C₂₀H₄₂: 2 × 20 + 2 = 42, so alkane; alkanes are saturated, with only single C–C bonds, each C forming four bonds and each H one bond; a hydrocarbon with fewer H than 2n + 2 must have a different structure (e.g. a double bond).
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): all four compounds correctly classified with reasons using both the hydrocarbon definition and CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, linked to saturated bonding.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): most compounds classified correctly with some reasons.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): one or two correct classifications with little reasoning.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Work in two steps: first check only C and H are present, then check the hydrogen count against 2n + 2. Only C₃H₈ and C₂₀H₄₂ pass both tests.

questions.question:
A hydrocarbon molecule contains 11 carbon atoms.
All the bonds in the molecule are single bonds.
What is the formula of the hydrocarbon?
markScheme: 1 mark: C₁₁H₂₄
questions.explanation: Only single bonds means it is an alkane: 2 × 11 + 2 = 24. C₁₁H₂₂ forgets the +2 and C₁₁H₂₆ adds too many.

questions.question:
Most of the compounds in crude oil are hydrocarbons.
Name the family of hydrocarbons that most of these compounds belong to.
markScheme: 1 mark: alkanes
questions.explanation: Most of the hydrocarbons in crude oil are alkanes.
